newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite IPE.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite IPE.

text.p: Singapore front-month gas oil swaps were steady midday on Tuesday despite large falls to futures prices on the IPE as the market found support in quiet trading at the $25.00-per-barrel mark, brokers said. "The market is steady in the absence of new factors. There is support at the $25.00 level," one broker said.

Gas oil swaps were last quoted largely unchanged from late Monday values at $25.05/$25.15 per barrel. The market lost about 70 cents on Monday from Friday's $25.75/$25.85 following large falls to crude, gas oil and heating oil futures on Friday.
February gas oil closed down 5.25 per tonne to $204.00 on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Monday.
Traders said the swaps market is finding it difficult to slip below the $25.00-per-barrel mark because physical buying interest emerges whenever cargoes are offered well below this level.
Last week several physical cargoes traded between $25.20 and $25.40 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore and on Monday an offer at $24.80 per barrel also drew buying buying interest.
On a floating price basis, physical cargoes last traded at about 30 cents discount to spot Singapore quotes on an fob basis.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted unchanged at $98.00/$99.00 per tonne in quiet trading.

Naphtha swaps edged up slightly despite steady crude prices as the market picked up on buying interest from Japan, brokers said. February swaps were last quoted at $24.35/$24.60 per barrel from Monday's $24.20/$24.60 per barrel, one broker said.
